_comment: bnw - hue removed AND mid-tones removed, so the glyphs stay legible.
This theme is not `mono`. Where mono keeps each key's shipped luminance and
only discards hue, bnw also flattens most of the greys and carries its
hierarchy by inversion - a black panel, a white field, black text on it.
The icons have to match that or they become the only soft, low-contrast
So: full grayscale first, then a contrast push around a 128 pivot. The
push is what removes the mid-tones. It is the icon-side equivalent of the
theme's four-tone palette, and it is why the opacity 1.0 icons survive as
crisp shapes instead of dissolving into grey.
The four-state flags (Square/Diamond/Cross/Check, on and off) are the most
contrast-sensitive icons in the set - they are distinguished from each
other by value alone, and a theme that compresses values makes them
ambiguous. Hence amount 1.7 rather than the 1.5 used for everything else.
25 of the 97 icons move. The other 72 cannot: 69 are pure white with alpha
and 3 are pure black, and `(255-128)*1.5+128` clamps straight back to 255
for both. A contrast op has nothing to do to a glyph that is already at an
extreme - which is why this theme, unlike `midnight` and `sunset`, leaves
the bulk of the icon set looking exactly as shipped.
